subject: Spanska
title: Grammar: irregular verbs in the present tense
sourceSummary: The common irregular verbs ir, tener, querer and hacer in the present tense.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Yo ___ al colegio en autobús." (ir = to go)
questions.opener: Ir is completely irregular: voy, vas, va...
questions.explanation: "Ir" conjugates: yo voy, tú vas, él/ella va, nosotros vamos, ellos van. "Yo" gives "voy".

questions.prompt: "Ir a + infinitive" is used to talk about the future, roughly like "going to". What does "Vamos a comer" mean?
questions.opener: The same construction as English's "going to".
questions.explanation: "Ir a + infinitive" describes something one is about to do: "vamos a comer" = "we are going to eat" (soon).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "¿Cuántos años ___ tú?" (tener = to have/to be ... years old)
questions.opener: Tener has an irregular stem with -ie- in some forms.
questions.explanation: "Tener" conjugates: yo tengo, tú tienes, él/ella tiene, nosotros tenemos, ellos tienen. "Tú" gives "tienes".

questions.opener: Spanish often uses "to have" where English/Swedish uses "to be".
questions.explanation: "Tener hambre" literally means "to have hunger", that is, "to be hungry". Likewise: "tener sed" (to be thirsty), "tener sueño" (to be sleepy), "tener prisa" (to be in a hurry).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Nosotros ___ los deberes por la tarde." (hacer = to do)
questions.opener: Hacer is regular in the "nosotros" form.
questions.explanation: "Hacer" conjugates: yo hago (irregular!), tú haces, él/ella hace, nosotros hacemos, ellos hacen. "Nosotros" gives "hacemos", which follows the regular -er pattern.

questions.prompt: Write the Spanish form of "querer" (to want) for "I": "Yo ___ un helado."
questions.opener: Querer has the same -ie- pattern as tener.

questions.prompt: Correct the two errors: "Yo tiene mucha hambre y quero comer algo."
questions.opener: Check the "I" form of both tener and querer.
questions.answer: Yo tengo mucha hambre y quiero comer algo.
steps: "Yo tiene" → "Yo tengo". Tener conjugates irregularly for "I" to "tengo", not "tiene" (which is for he/she).
"Quero" → "quiero". Querer has -ie- in the stem for "I": "quiero", not "quero".
The full sentence: "Yo tengo mucha hambre y quiero comer algo." (I am very hungry and want to eat something.)

questions.prompt: How are ir, tener, querer and hacer conjugated in the present tense?
questions.opener: Four of the most common irregular verbs.
questions.answer: Ir (to go): voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. Ir a + infinitive = going to do something (future). Tener (to have): tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. Used in expressions like tener hambre/sed/sueño/prisa (to be hungry/thirsty/sleepy/in a hurry). Querer (to want): quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren. Hacer (to do/make): hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen — only the "yo" form is irregular.
